historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgement: FY2026 base-year growth. H1 FY2026 revenue +7.1% YoY (AI retail core solution +24.0%, value-added services slower with a hardware mix shift), decelerating from +19.8% in FY2025; NRR 112%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Only FY2023-FY2025 are in the Metrics history (three annual periods), so 3- and 5-year CAGRs cannot be computed. Equity CAGR is meaningless (net liabilities of -6.9bn in FY2023 from preferred-share liabilities, +899m after the IPO conversion); EPS was negative in FY2023-FY2024 and owner FCF turned positive only in FY2025 (-199 -> -111 -> +93). The 2-year revenue CAGR of 18.5% is above the current run-rate and is not used as the forward anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income (leases charged in the forward build). FY2023 interest income is not disclosed in the context lines; the FY2024 figure (8.5) is used as a proxy. SBC grew 13.6 -> 19.3 -> 31.5 (0.9% -> 1.0% -> 1.4% of revenue), faster than revenue, but it remains small by US-SaaS standards.

scenario_narratives.base: Dmall grows 8-9% near term on AI core-solution expansion and >100% NRR, with value-added services (hardware-heavy, Wumart-concentrated) growing slowly; adjusted EBITDA margin climbs from ~10.5% to 15% over a decade as the subscription/AI mix rises and AI-assisted R&D holds opex growth below revenue. Cash tax stays near zero for three years on tax losses then ramps to 17%. Working capital consumes ~4% of incremental revenue (related-party receivables). WACC 10% in CNY, terminal growth 2.5%, Gordon binds below the 15x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The retail-AI-agents pivot monetises: the ten AI modules move from RMB64m to a material revenue-share stream, overseas benchmark projects (DFI, SM Group, Cold Storage Singapore, Middle East) compound at 20%+, and independent Chinese chains (7-Eleven China, Tangjiu) diversify the base away from Wumart. Growth re-accelerates to 14% in FY2027-28 and the margin reaches 20% by year 9; terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Related-party dependence becomes the ceiling: Wumart-affiliated spend flattens, the ownership overhang keeps competitors' chains off the platform, larger platform rivals compress pricing, and revenue stalls from FY2027 while the margin slides back to ~9%. The stablecoin/Bitcoin side-venture absorbs capital and attention. Terminal growth 1.5%; the business remains cash-generative but is worth little more than its net cash plus a low-growth annuity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on the post-IPO run-rate: SBC expensed and the diluted count held flat, interest income stripped against a net-cash bridge that also carries the FVPL wealth-management assets and deducts NCI, leases charged as operating cost, cash tax ramped from zero to a PRC high-tech rate, and working capital charged on the revenue change. The pre-IPO preferred-share fair-value losses are capital-structure noise and are excluded from the operating history; the valuation rests on whether the H1 FY2026 margin step-up (~11% adjusted EBITDA, +66% profit on +7% revenue) is the start of a SaaS-style margin ramp or a cyclical high in a related-party revenue base.
key_risks_to_valuation: Related-party concentration: Wumart/Wumei entities fund the bulk of subscription revenue; a change in the anchor's trading or ownership moves the whole base case
Revenue deceleration already visible (+19.8% FY2025 -> +7.1% H1 FY2026); the base case assumes a modest re-acceleration that the value-added segment may not deliver
Margin ramp risk: gross margin fell to 37.2% in H1 FY2026 on hardware mix; the 15% EBITDA target depends on AI/subscription mix, not on cost cuts that have already been taken

Capital allocation: Bitcoin purchases, a crypto-fund FVPL position and a planned stablecoin licence are outside the core thesis and sit in a company that also raised equity at HK$11.10 in July 2025 and is buying back below that
Cash tax: the model ramps to 17%; an earlier exhaustion of tax losses or loss of high-tech status (25% statutory) lowers value
FX: a CNY-built value translated at CNY/HKD 1.173; a 5% RMB move shifts the HKD value by the same amount, and refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (2586.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.78-9.68. Fresh build, no prior DCF.
data_sources.financials: research/2586.HK/Reports/2586.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2023-H1 FY2026, RMB millions) and the extracted filings: 2586.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (cash-flow statement, adjusted-profit reconciliation, share plans) and 2586.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (balance sheet, cash flow, EPS note 7, FVPL note 19, treasury-share and buyback disclosures, borrowings maturity).
data_sources.fx: Yahoo CNYHKD=X on 2026-10-16, cross-checked against USDHKD/USDCNY.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 937,510,811 shares in issue incl. treasury (H1 FY2026 interim) less 67,366,800 treasury shares = 870,144,011 outstanding, plus 4,664,631 treasury-method dilution from the H1 FY2026 diluted-EPS denominator (note 7(c)). Gross award overhang is larger (2016 options 28.3m, 2020 options 27.4m, 2020 RSUs 3.9m, 2024 second awards/options 6.0m) but most options are out of the money at the current price. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the July 2026 repurchase of 4,072,200 shares (RMB21.4m, after the balance-sheet date) is not netted because the cash was still on the June 30 balance sheet.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, adjusted-profit reconciliation (equity-settled share-based payment expenses RMB31,457k); H1 FY2026 interim RMB14,303k. No equity-award cash taxes disclosed (net-share settlement not used); EquityAwardTaxes = 0.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases RMB196.9m; H1 FY2026 RMB343.2m (56.5m shares at HK$5.62-9.00, held as treasury). The flat count is being funded in cash, well beyond the SBC charge; the surplus buyback is treated as value-neutral capital return.
inputs.owner_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported FCF 146.129 - SBC 31.457 - interest income 22.031 = 92.641 (contract identity). Lease cash (FY2025 capital element 24.407 + interest 0.973 = 25.380) is charged in the forward build via lease_cost_pct_path, so the like-for-like FY0 owner FCF is 67.3. FY2025 reported capex (45.845) includes RMB41.4m of Bitcoin purchases booked as intangible-asset additions and disposed within the year into a crypto fund (FVPL); true operating capex was RMB4.5m PP&E. The reported figure is kept as the conservative base; forward capex_pct reflects PP&E plus the capitalised development costs that began in H1 FY2026 (RMB18.4m).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. Per-share values computed in CNY and converted at CNY/HKD 1.173 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X 1.1724 on 2026-10-16; cross-check USDHKD 7.8479 / USDCNY 6.6862 = 1.1737). No dual listing for a parity check; the July 2026 buyback disclosure (HK$24.6m = RMB21.4m, i.e. 1.150) confirms the direction and is within the rate's drift since then.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank loans and other borrowings 380.937 current + 55.600 non-current = 436.537 (2.45-3.0% p.a.); cash and cash equivalents 653.563 (restricted deposits 0.618 excluded). Lease liabilities (33.747) excluded under lease treatment (B). Current FVPL financial assets (wealth-management products 86.602 + fund investment 19.352 = 105.954) are added in the equity bridge, not in cash. Net cash of 217 is >2x the FCF base, so interest income is stripped from the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: WACC 10.0% built in CNY: PRC 10-year CGB ~1.8% risk-free, China ERP incl. country risk ~6.3%, beta ~1.3 for a small-cap HK-listed China SaaS name -> cost of equity ~10%; debt is <10% of capital at 2.5-3.0% pre-tax, rounding WACC to 10.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: customer concentration, AI-pivot execution and governance risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: full lease payment (capital element + interest, both on the cash-flow statement; FY2025 25.4m = 1.14% of revenue, H1 FY2026 11.4m = 0.99%) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (PP&E depreciation ex-ROU ~6m + intangible amortisation ~30m = ~1.5% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; NCI book value (65.852 at 2026-06-30) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI subsidiaries are loss-making (NCI share -6.6m FY2025, -5.3m H1 FY2026), so attributable profit exceeds total profit and deducting book is the conservative side.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA before SBC, before lease cash (post-IFRS-16), excluding other net income/loss (FVPL fair-value changes, Guoquan gains, government grants) and the FY2025 goodwill impairment (45.7). FY2025 ~10.1%; H1 FY2026 ~11.2% (profit from operations 78.2 + D&A 29.8 + SBC 14.3 + other net loss 6.9 = 129.2 on revenue 1,154.5).
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax paid is ~zero (FY2025 0.135m; H1 FY2026 0.12m) on accumulated tax losses, and the P&L shows income-tax BENEFITS from deferred-tax-asset recognition (28.9m in H1 FY2026). Cash tax ramps from 0% to the 15% PRC high-tech-enterprise rate plus dividend-withholding leakage (17% base, 20% bear, 15% bull) by year 6.
inputs.wc_note: Working capital consumes cash with growth: trade receivables 312m (13.6% of revenue, largely related-party) + inventories 1.1% exceed contract liabilities 5.8% + trade payables 4.9%; net ~4% of revenue, so wc_capture_pct = -4 on the revenue change.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 1, operating SaaS/retail-tech company) with the non-US adaptations: CNY-built WACC, CNY->HKD bridge, lease treatment (B), NCI in the bridge, FVPL assets matched to the stripped investment income. Routed as an operating company despite the short profit record: FY2023-FY2024 net losses were dominated by non-cash fair-value losses on pre-IPO convertible redeemable preferred shares (-476m, -2,276m) that converted to equity at the December 2024 IPO; operating income turned positive in FY2025 (85.4) and H1 FY2026 (78.2), so the forward flows are built from the post-IPO run-rate, not from the loss history. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry).

bear.narrative: Wumart/Wumei-affiliated spend (the bulk of value-added-service subscriptions) flattens as the anchor retailer's own trading softens, competing chains keep refusing a Wumart-owned platform, and Alibaba/JD/Yonyou price pressure caps independent wins: revenue stalls after FY2026, the margin slips back to ~9% as hardware mix and AI model costs rise, and management attention and cash leak into the stablecoin/crypto initiative. Terminal growth 1.5%.

base.narrative: FY2026 +8% on the H1 run-rate, re-accelerating modestly to 9% in FY2027-28 as AI core-solution growth (+24% in H1 FY2026) outweighs the slower hardware-heavy value-added services, then tapering to 3% by year 10. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands from ~10.5% to 15% as subscription/AI mix rises and AI-assisted R&D holds opex growth below revenue; cash tax ramps from zero to 17% by year 6 as tax losses are used.

bull.narrative: AI agent modules (RMB64m of AI revenue in FY2025) scale into revenue-share contracts, overseas (DFI, SM Group, Cold Storage, Middle East) grows from 9% toward a quarter of revenue, and non-Wumart logos keep NRR above 110%: growth re-accelerates to 14% and the margin reaches a 20% SaaS-like level by year 9. Tax settles at the 15% high-tech rate with the HK treaty withholding.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% for a single-customer-group dependency (Wumart/Wumei related entities supply ~92% of value-added subscription revenue), a profit record of only six half-years post-IPO, a controlling shareholder who is also the anchor customer, and an unproven AI-agents pivot layered with a stablecoin/crypto diversification. Bull cut to 20% because it needs AI monetisation, overseas scaling and non-Wumart wins to all come through together. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
